vulnerability.category_l2: SSRF allowlist bypass: incomplete private-subnet list omits IPv6 transition prefixes that embed private IPv4 addresses

critical_operation.description: NoPrivateNetworkHttpClient::request() installs an on_progress callback that blocks the request when the resolved primary_ip matches $subnets ?? PRIVATE_SUBNETS via IpUtils::checkIp(). At v5.4.45 PRIVATE_SUBNETS lists only RFC1918, loopback, link-local, 0/8, 240/4, fc00::/7, fe80::/10, ::ffff:0:0/96 and ::/128; it omits the IPv6 transition forms that embed an IPv4 destination: IPv4-compatible ::/96, 6to4 2002::/16, Teredo 2001::/32, and NAT64 64:ff9b::/96 and 64:ff9b:1::/48. checkIp() compares bits against the list and never extracts the embedded IPv4, so an attacker-supplied URL such as http://[2002:7f00:1::]/ that encodes 127.0.0.1 passes the guard and reaches the private target. The 5.4.53 fix adds the five prefixes.

entry_point.description: An application passes an attacker-controlled URL to a NoPrivateNetworkHttpClient instance, e.g. a webhook, image fetch or link-preview feature.

trace.description: PRIVATE_SUBNETS lists 12 CIDR blocks and omits all IPv6 transition prefixes
the on_progress callback checks primary_ip against the incomplete list
the request is delegated to the wrapped client once the guard passes

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No HTTP request, DNS resolution or SSRF payload was executed; the bypass is verified statically and was not reproduced.
The 5.4 file was refactored between v5.4.45 and v5.4.53, so the full-file diff includes unrelated changes; the security-relevant change is the constant.
The second fix commit 85b83155 targets IpUtils on 6.4+ and is not part of the 5.4 tree; only 82765368 was checked against v5.4.53 ancestry.
CNA 4.0 6.9 Medium and NVD Primary 3.1 8.6 High disagree materially (the latter has scope changed and C:H).
open_questions: Whether other consumers of IpUtils::checkIp on 5.4 (outside this client) also missed the transition forms was not audited.
Whether the on_progress timing allows any connection side effect before the exception is thrown was not analysed.
